mainTopic: Which services make a זר liable to מיתה (inside, outside, and in the היכל; עבודה תמה), and the details of the daily lotteries
overview: This amud continues the discussion of which Temple services make a זר (non-כהן) liable to מיתה. From the פסוק "ולמבית לפרוכת ועבדתם", the גמרא learns that the rule 'only עבודת מתנה, not עבודת סילוק' applies only inside. Outside, even a removal service makes a זר liable. The ו of "ועבדתם" shows that the rule of עבודה תמה applies both inside and outside. רבא asks whether the היכל counts as inside or outside, and he answers from the extra letters of "ולמבית" that it counts as inside. The גמרא then tests this rule on the שלחן, the מנורה, and the מערכה on the altar. Each step turns out to be incomplete, except lighting the מנורה, which is not an עבודה at all. רב and רבי יוחנן disagree about the two logs, and a ברייתא is brought supporting each of רב and לוי. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה's lotteries. רבי יוחנן explains that they were repeated to stir up the עזרה. רב נחמן and רב ששת then argue about whether the כהנים wore weekday or holy clothes for the lottery.

steps.title: The removal exemption applies only inside the veil
steps.stepSummary: From "אל מבית לפרוכת", only inside the קודש הקדשים is a זר liable just for עבודת מתנה and not for עבודת סילוק. Outside, even עבודת סילוק makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "and to within the veil, and you shall serve." It is "to within the veil" that only a giving-service counts, and not a removal-service. This implies that outside, even a removal-service counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the פסוק so that the exemption for removal services is limited to the קודש הקדשים. This explains how a זר can be liable for a removal service outside, such as removing the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "עבודת מתנה" in the פסוק teach that only giving-type services bring מיתה. The words "אל מבית לפרוכת" limit that rule to the קודש הקדשים. So outside, the limit falls away, and even a סילוק service makes a זר liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the curtain, meaning the קודש הקדשים
A 'giving' service that places something onto the altar, such as sprinkling blood or burning incense
A 'removal' service that takes something away, such as removing the incense pan or the ashes
This implies that outside the curtain the rule is different
A non-כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that a removal service is not a real עבודה. It is still Temple service. The only question is whether a זר gets מיתה for it, and the answer depends on where it is done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole structure of the sugya. Location (inside or outside the veil) decides whether a removal service brings מיתה.

phrases.notes: The verse continues: "עבודת מתנה אתן את כהונתכם"

phrases.english: it is "to within the veil"
phrases.notes: This part of the verse is only talking about the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: that a giving-service brings liability

phrases.notes: For example, taking out the כף and מחתה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation from the previous daf that explains how a זר can be liable for a removal service outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption for עבודת סילוק applies only inside the קודש הקדשים. Outside, a זר is liable even for a removal service.

steps.title: Then the complete-service rule should also apply only inside
steps.stepSummary: If "אל מבית לפרוכת" limits the giving-service rule, it should also limit the rule from "ועבדתם" that only a עבודה תמה brings liability. Then outside, even an incomplete service would bring מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, "and you shall serve" should also be limited: it is only "to within the veil" that a complete service counts and not a service that has another service after it. This would imply that outside, even a service with another service after it counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 1. If "within the veil" limits one rule, it should limit the other rule in the same פסוק too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from "ועבדתם" that a זר is liable only for a complete service, one that is not followed by another service that finishes the job. By the logic of step 1, "אל מבית לפרוכת" should restrict that rule to the inside as well. That would give the unacceptable result that outside, a זר gets מיתה even for incomplete, preparatory services.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the previous claim)
A complete service that finishes its purpose on its own
A service that has another service after it, meaning it is preparatory or incomplete
"And you shall serve", the source for the complete-service rule

phrases.english: If so, "and you shall serve" also
phrases.notes: So this word should also be limited to "within the veil."

phrases.english: it is "to within the veil"
that a complete service brings liability
and not a service that has another service after it.
This would imply that outside,
even a service that has another service after it brings liability!
phrases.notes: And that can't be right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 1 by applying the same logic to the other limitation in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that "אל מבית לפרוכת" limits the rules in the פסוק to the inside only.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consistency: if the location phrase limits the giving-service rule, it should also limit the complete-service rule. That would make a זר liable outside even for incomplete services, which is unacceptable.

steps.title: The vav of ועבדתם joins inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: The extra ו in "ועבדתם" joins the outside services back together with the inside ones. So the עבודה תמה rule applies everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall serve": the verse went back and joined them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word "ועבדתם" begins with "and", which links the inside and outside together for the complete-service rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו ("and") signals that the פסוק returns and joins the outside services to the inside ones. So the complete-service rule is not limited by "אל מבית לפרוכת". The giving-service rule, which has no such joining word, stays limited to the inside, as step 1 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back, returned
Combined it, joined it together
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Outside the veil, a זר is liable even for עבודת סילוק, but only for a complete service. Inside, he is liable only for עבודת מתנה, and also only for a complete service.

phrases.english: "And you shall serve"
phrases.notes: The ו ("and") is the key

phrases.english: the verse went back and joined them together.
phrases.notes: Inside and outside are the same for this rule

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: a ו connector shows the rule extends to both areas
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The location phrase limits every rule in the פסוק to the inside, so outside even incomplete services would be punishable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו of "ועבדתם" joins outside to inside, so the complete-service rule applies everywhere. Only the giving-service limit is restricted to the inside.

steps.title: רבא asks about a removal service in the היכל
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a עבודת סילוק done in the היכל (between the קודש הקדשים and the outside) is treated like inside, where there is no liability, or like outside, where there is liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What is the law for a removal-service in the היכל? Do we compare it to inside, or do we compare it to outside?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question based on the rule just established. He opens a new line of discussion that the גמרא will go on to address.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have two clear zones. Inside the veil, removal brings no מיתה; outside, it does. The היכל is a middle area: it is inside the building but outside the פרוכת. Examples of removal there are clearing the inner altar or cleaning the מנורה. רבא wants to know which zone the היכל belongs to for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question or dilemma
The Sanctuary room in front of the קודש הקדשים, containing the מנורה, שלחן, and inner altar
What is the law?
Do we compare it?

steps.confusionAlert: "לפנים" here means the קודש הקדשים, and "לחוץ" means the courtyard. The היכל is the area in between.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
a removal-service in the Heichal, what is the law?
phrases.notes: For example, removing the burnt incense from the inner altar

phrases.english: Do we compare it to inside,
phrases.notes: Then there would be no מיתה

phrases.english: or do we compare it to outside?
phrases.notes: Then there would be מיתה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inside/outside rule to ask about a middle area.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a זר who does a removal service in the היכל is liable to מיתה, depending on whether the היכל is treated like inside or outside.

steps.title: רבא answers: the extra 'and' adds the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves his question. 'מבית' alone would mean only the קודש הקדשים. 'ולמבית' adds the היכל, so the היכל follows the inside rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא went back and answered it himself: the verse could have said 'within,' but it says 'and to within.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question he asked in Step 4. He shows from an extra letter in the פסוק that the היכל is treated like the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מבית' by itself would cover only the קודש הקדשים. The added ו and ל in 'ולמבית' include one more place, the היכל. So in the היכל, a זר is liable only for a complete service, just as inside, and not for a עבודת סילוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and resolved it himself
'Within', which alone means only the קודש הקדשים
'And to within', where the extra letters add the היכל

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the rest of this passage tests: in the היכל, only a final, complete service makes a זר liable.

phrases.english: He went back and resolved it:
phrases.notes: רבא answers his own question from Step 4.

phrases.english: 'Within' — 'and to within.'
phrases.notes: The verse does not just say 'within'; it says 'and to within,' which adds the היכל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבא raised in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the היכל is treated like inside or like outside
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The היכל is like inside, learned from the extra letters in 'ולמבית'.

steps.title: Challenge: a non-כהן who arranges the table should be liable
steps.stepSummary: If a זר is liable for a complete service in the היכל, then arranging the לחם הפנים on the שלחן should make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a non-כהן who arranged the table should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new rule with a case. Arranging the bread on the שלחן is done in the היכל, so a זר who does it should be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arranging the bread looks like a placing service that happens in the היכל. If the new rule is right, the גמרא expects liability here. This opens a chain of challenges.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a challenge based on what was just said)
The table in the היכל that holds the לחם הפנים
He should be liable

phrases.english: But if so,
phrases.notes: Takes the new rule and pushes it further.

phrases.english: a non-כהן who arranged the table
phrases.notes: He set the לחם הפנים on the שלחן.

phrases.english: should be liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule from Step 5 on a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a זר is liable for a giving service in the היכל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arranging the bread is a placing service in the היכל, so the rule predicts liability.

steps.title: Answer: the frankincense bowls still need to be arranged
steps.stepSummary: Arranging the bread is not the final step, because the בזיכין of frankincense still have to be set out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the arranging of the bowls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that arranging the bread is not a complete service, because another step still remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability needs a complete, final service. After the bread is arranged, the בזיכין of לבונה still have to be placed, so the job is not finished.

keyTerms.meaning: There is still
Arranging the two bowls of frankincense next to the bread

phrases.english: There is still the arranging of the bowls.
phrases.notes: So the bread arranging is not the final, complete service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the act is not a complete service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Arranging the bread finishes a service
steps.terutzMaskana: Another step (the בזיכין) remains, so there is no liability

steps.title: Challenge: then arranging the bowls should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: If the bowls are the next step, then a זר who arranges the בזיכין should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he arranged the bowls, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next step in the process and asks whether that one makes a זר liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bread arranging failed only because the bowls were still missing, then placing the bowls might be the final step.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged
Frankincense, which is in the בזיכין

phrases.english: If he arranged the bowls,
he should be liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the answer of Step 7 one step further.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bowls are the missing step, placing them should complete the service.

steps.title: Answer: removing the bowls and burning still remain
steps.stepSummary: Arranging the bowls is not final either. Later they are removed and the frankincense is burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the removing and the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that arranging the bowls is still not the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The frankincense must later be taken off the שלחן and burned. Since that remains, arranging the bowls is not a complete service, and there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing the bowls from the table
Burning the frankincense on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: For the שלחן, neither arranging the bread nor arranging the bowls is a complete service, because later steps still remain.

phrases.english: There is still the removing and the burning.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the act is not a complete service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Arranging the bowls finishes the service
steps.terutzMaskana: Removal and burning still follow, so there is no liability

steps.title: Challenge: arranging the מנורה should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a זר who arranges the lamps of the מנורה should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-כהן who arranged the מנורה should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the same rule on a second object in the היכל, the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting up the lamps is a service done in the היכל. The גמרא asks whether it counts as a complete service.

keyTerms.meaning: The candelabrum in the היכל
Set up the lamps of the מנורה

phrases.english: A non-כהן who arranged the Menorah
should be liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new test case, parallel to the שלחן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arranging the lamps is a service in the היכל, so the rule predicts liability.

steps.title: Answer: the wicks still need to be put in
steps.stepSummary: Arranging the lamps is not final, because the wicks still have to be placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the placing of the wick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that setting up the lamps is not the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wick still has to go in, so this is not a complete service and there is no liability.

steps.title: Challenge: then placing the wick should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: If the wick is the next step, a זר who places it should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he placed the wick, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next step for the מנורה and asks again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא asks whether placing the wick finishes the service.

keyTerms.meaning: He placed or put in

phrases.english: If he placed the wick,

steps.title: Answer: the oil still needs to be poured
steps.stepSummary: Placing the wick is not final, because the oil still has to be added.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the placing of the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wick is still not the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil must still be poured in, so placing the wick is not a complete service.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring in the oil

phrases.english: There is still the placing of the oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placing the wick finishes the service
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is still missing, so there is no liability

steps.title: Challenge: then pouring the oil should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: If oil is the next step, a זר who pours it should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he placed the oil, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next step and asks whether pouring the oil finishes the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After wick and oil, the lamp seems ready. So the גמרא asks whether this is the final act.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil for the מנורה

phrases.english: If he placed the oil,
he should be liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the answer of Step 13 one step further.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If oil was the missing step, pouring it should complete the service.

steps.title: Answer: the lighting still remains
steps.stepSummary: Pouring the oil is not final, because the lamps still have to be lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the lighting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the oil is still not the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamps still need to be lit, so pouring the oil is not a complete service.

keyTerms.meaning: Lighting the lamps

phrases.english: There is still the lighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the act is not a complete service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring the oil finishes the service
steps.terutzMaskana: The lighting still remains, so there is no liability

steps.title: Challenge: then lighting should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: Lighting is clearly the last step, so a זר who lights the lamps should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lit it, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the very last step in the process. Nothing comes after lighting, so it seems this must bring liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting cannot be answered with 'there is still another step,' because it is the last act. This is the strongest challenge in the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: He lit

phrases.english: If he lit it,
he should be liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the answer of Step 15 to the final step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lighting is the final act, so it should be a complete service that brings liability.

steps.title: Answer: lighting is not a Temple service at all
steps.stepSummary: Lighting the מנורה does not count as an עבודה, so a זר who lights is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lighting is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new kind of answer. Lighting is not too early in the process; it simply does not count as an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now every answer was 'another step remains.' Here the answer changes: lighting is not a real Temple service, because nothing is done to the מנורה itself. Since it is not an עבודה, a זר may light it and is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a real Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: In the היכל, a זר is liable only for a complete, final עבודה. Arranging the bread, the bowls, the lamps, the wick, and the oil are all unfinished steps. Lighting is the last step, but it is not an עבודה at all.
steps.confusionAlert: The last answer works differently from the earlier ones. Lighting is not exempt because another step remains. It is exempt because it is not considered an עבודה in the first place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that lighting the מנורה is valid even when done by a זר.

phrases.english: Lighting
is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 with a new kind of answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the act as not an עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lighting is the final, complete service, so a זר should be liable
steps.terutzMaskana: Lighting is not an עבודה at all, so there is no liability
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule from Step 5 holds. None of the מנורה or שלחן steps make a זר liable.

steps.title: Isn't kindling fire a real service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that kindling is not an עבודה. A ברייתא says kindling the chips on the altar must be done by a fit כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it really not a service? But a ברייתא teaches: 'And the sons of אהרן the כהן shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.' This teaches that kindling the chips may only be done by a fit כהן and with a כלי שרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer, which said lighting is not an עבודה. It brings a ברייתא showing that lighting a fire on the altar is treated as a real עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said lighting is not an עבודה, so a זר who lights is exempt. But the ברייתא learns from a פסוק that kindling the altar's fire requires a fit כהן. That sounds like a full עבודה, so how can lighting be 'not an עבודה'?

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge from a source)
Kindling the chips or kindling wood used to light the altar fire
A כהן who is fit to serve
A sacred service vessel (some explain it here as the priestly garments)

phrases.english: And is it not [a service]? But wasn't it taught:
"And the sons of Aharon the priest shall put
fire upon the altar
and arrange wood upon the fire"
this teaches about kindling the chips
that it may only be done by a fit priest
and with a service vessel!
phrases.notes: Some read this as 'priestly garments' instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 17 that lighting is not an עבודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that lighting (הדלקה) is not an עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires a fit כהן to kindle the altar fire, which shows that kindling is an עבודה.

steps.title: Altar kindling is a service; lighting the מנורה is not
steps.stepSummary: Kindling the altar's fire is an עבודה. Lighting the מנורה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kindling the chips on the altar is a service. Lighting the מנורה is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the two kinds of lighting. The altar fire counts as an עבודה, but the מנורה lighting does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke only about the altar fire. The earlier answer in step 17 was about lighting the מנורה. So step 17 still stands: a זר who lights the מנורה is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Lighting (here, lighting the מנורה)
A formal Temple service
Not

steps.confusionAlert: Both acts involve fire, but they are not the same. Only kindling the altar's fire counts as a formal עבודה. Lighting the מנורה does not.

phrases.english: Kindling the chips is a service;
lighting [the menorah] is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All kindling of fire in the מקדש is one category of עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Altar kindling is an עבודה. מנורה lighting is not, so a זר who lights the מנורה is exempt.

steps.title: Then a non-כהן who sets up the woodpile should be liable
steps.stepSummary: If placing actions can make a זר liable, then arranging the altar's woodpile should make him liable too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a זר who arranged the woodpile on the altar should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the rule on a new case: setting up the מערכה, the main woodpile on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said a זר is liable for a placing action if it is the final step. Arranging the woodpile seems like a placing action. So why isn't a זר liable for it?

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so (introduces a challenge that follows from the last answer)
The arranged woodpile on the altar
A non-כהן
He should be liable

phrases.english: But now, if so,
a non-priest who arranged the woodpile
should be liable!

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a זר is liable for a final placing action.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arranging the מערכה is a placing action, so it should also make a זר liable.

steps.title: The two logs still have to be added
steps.stepSummary: Arranging the woodpile is not the final step, because the two logs still have to be placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the arranging of two logs of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the woodpile is not a complete service. Another step comes after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the main woodpile is set up, two extra logs are placed on the altar. Since more work follows, arranging the woodpile is not an עבודה תמה.

keyTerms.meaning: There is (still)
Two logs of wood placed on the altar

phrases.english: There is [still] the arranging of two logs of wood.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Arranging the woodpile is a complete placing action.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two logs come after it, so it is not complete.

steps.title: Then a non-כהן who places the two logs should be liable
steps.stepSummary: If the two logs come next, then placing them should make a זר liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a זר who arranged the two logs should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves one step down the chain and asks about the two logs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern as before. If the last answer said the two logs are the next step, maybe they are the final step. If so, a זר who places them should be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranged
Logs

phrases.english: If he arranged the two logs, he should be liable!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing the two logs seems to be the final placing action, so it should make a זר liable.

steps.title: The limbs still have to be placed
steps.stepSummary: Placing the two logs is not final, because the limbs of the offerings are placed on the fire afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is still the arranging of the limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even the two logs are followed by another step: putting the limbs of the קרבנות on the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the limbs are arranged after the logs, the logs are not an עבודה תמה. This ends the chain on the altar, following רב's rule that only his four services make a זר liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranging the limbs of the offerings on the altar fire
Limbs (of a קרבן)

phrases.english: There is [still] the arranging of the limbs.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two logs are the last step.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limbs are placed after the logs, so the logs are not complete.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the two logs do make a non-כהן liable
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: a זר who arranged the two logs is liable. This contradicts step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב אסי say in the name of רבי יוחנן: a זר who arranged the two logs of wood is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי יוחנן that says the opposite of the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said placing the two logs is not complete, so a זר is exempt. רבי יוחנן clearly says a זר is liable for it. That also conflicts with רב's list of only four services.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (opens a challenge from an אמורא)
An אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's teaching
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
Liable

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Asi say that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זָר שֶׁסִּידֵּר שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים חַיָּיב!
phrases.english: a non-priest who arranged the two logs of wood is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 23 and רב's list of four services.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An authority states outright that a זר is liable for the two logs.

steps.title: רב and רבי יוחנן disagree about the two logs
steps.stepSummary: The two disagree on whether placing the two logs counts as a complete service.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this. One holds it is a complete service, and the other holds it is not a complete service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not try to reconcile the two views. It says they simply disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds the two logs are an עבודה תמה. In his view, arranging the limbs is a separate act, not part of the wood setup. רב holds they are not complete, because the limbs come after them, so a זר is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree on this point
One authority holds
A complete service, with no further step after it

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of עבודה תמה is the key test running through this whole section. This step shows that its exact boundaries are disputed.

phrases.english: On this they disagree:
one Sage holds it is a complete service,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָאו עֲבוֹדָה תַּמָּה הִיא.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds it is not a complete service.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and רב must agree on this point.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree: רבי יוחנן says the two logs are complete, and רב says they are not.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting both רב and לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רב and another supports לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב, and a ברייתא was taught in line with לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא goes back to the original dispute between רב and לוי and gets ready to quote a source for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counted four services that make a זר liable. לוי added תרומת הדשן, removing the ashes. The גמרא will now show that each view has support in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in line with him
The אמורא who counts four services
The אמורא who adds תרומת הדשן

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav,
it was taught in accordance with Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עבודה תמה discussion and returns to the רב and לוי dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each view, רב's and לוי's, has a supporting ברייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא listing services that matches רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists sprinkling blood, burning, and the water and wine libations. It does not mention removing the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא in line with רב: These are the services for which a זר is liable to death: sprinkling blood, whether inside the היכל or in the קודש הקדשים; one who sprinkles the blood of a חטאת העוף; one who squeezes out the blood of an עולת העוף or burns it; and one who pours three לוגין of water or three לוגין of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that supports רב. It lists only the kinds of service that רב counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the items fit into רב's four groups: blood services, burning, water libation, and wine libation. תרומת הדשן is missing from the list. That supports רב against לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Death at the hands of Heaven
Throwing or sprinkling the blood of a קרבן
The innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים
A bird sin-offering
One who squeezes out the blood onto the altar wall
A liquid measure (plural of לוג)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's list matches רב's four services and leaves out תרומת הדשן. This is support for רב. Next, the גמרא will bring a ברייתא for לוי.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
Services for which a non-priest is liable to death:
sprinkling of blood, whether inside
or in the innermost chamber;
and one who sprinkles in a bird sin-offering;
and one who squeezes out or burns a bird burnt-offering;
and one who pours three log of water,
or three log of wine.

steps.raayaObject: רב's view that only four services make a זר liable, without תרומת הדשן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the services that make a זר liable to death.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports Levi
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the services a זר is killed for doing, and it includes removing the ashes. This supports לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with לוי. These are the services that a non-כהן is liable to death for doing: removing the ashes, the seven sprinklings done inside, the sprinklings of a מצורע, and bringing something up onto the מזבח, whether it is a kosher item or a disqualified one.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 26 promised two ברייתות. Step 27 brought the one that supports רב, and this is the second one, which supports לוי. This list includes הרמת הדשן, removing the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument is about whether תרומת הדשן is a real service that carries the death penalty for a זר. The ברייתא in step 27 left it out, which fits רב. This ברייתא lists it first, which fits לוי, so each opinion has a תנא behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
A non-כהן
One who removes the ashes (תרומת הדשן)
Sprinklings
A person with the skin disease צרעת

steps.whatToRemember: רב: תרומת הדשן is not a death-penalty service for a זר. לוי: it is. Each opinion is backed by its own ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Levi:
Services for which a non-priest is liable to death:
one who removes the ashes,
phrases.notes: This item is the reason the ברייתא supports לוי.

phrases.english: and the seven sprinklings that are inside,
and those of the leper,
and one who brings up onto the altar

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דָּבָר כָּשֵׁר בֵּין דָּבָר פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: whether a valid item or a disqualified item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the pair of supporting ברייתות promised in step 26
steps.raayaObject: לוי's view that a זר who does תרומת הדשן is liable to death
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists הרמת הדשן among the death-penalty services

steps.title: Why hold lotteries?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the daily lotteries and asks why they were held.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they hold lotteries?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the רב and לוי topic and returns to the משנה about the פייס. It opens with a simple question, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question as asked seems to want the basic reason for having a lottery at all. The very next step will show that this cannot be what the question means.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold a lottery (פייס) to assign the services

phrases.english: Why do they hold lotteries?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה

steps.title: The question is already answered in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question, because the משנה already explained why there was a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do they hold lotteries?! It is as we said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. The משנה already told us the reason: to avoid fights and danger among the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question that the משנה clearly answered cannot be the real question. So the wording of step 29 must mean something else, and the next step will explain what.

keyTerms.meaning: As we already said

steps.confusionAlert: The same words, למה מפייסין, appear twice in a row. The first time is a question. The second time is the גמרא saying in surprise: 'How can you ask that?!'

phrases.english: Why do they hold lotteries?!
phrases.notes: Said in surprise, not as a real question

phrases.english: As we said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 29 makes sense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already gave the reason for the lottery, so there is no need to ask.

steps.title: The real question: why several separate lotteries?
steps.stepSummary: The question is restated: why gather the כהנים for a lottery again and again, instead of doing all the lotteries at once?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: why do they hold a lottery, and then come back and hold another lottery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the question. The issue is not why there was a lottery at all. It is why there were several separate gatherings for lotteries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes four lotteries spread through the morning. All the assignments could have been decided at one gathering, so there must be a reason for repeating it. That reason is what step 32 will give.

keyTerms.meaning: And they come back and hold a lottery again

phrases.english: Rather:
why do they hold a lottery and then again hold a lottery?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30 by changing what the question means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question asked why there was any lottery at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question asks why the lottery was repeated several times.

steps.title: To create a stir in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the repeated gatherings were meant to create excitement throughout the עזרה, and he supports this with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: to stir up the whole courtyard, as it says: 'Together we took sweet counsel; in the House of God we walked with a throng.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the corrected question. Each new gathering made the כהנים rush in from all over, which filled the עזרה with lively activity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the lottery was done on purpose, not because it was efficient. The פסוק shows that a bustling crowd in the בית המקדש is a good and fitting thing.

keyTerms.meaning: To stir up, to create a commotion
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
With a throng, with excitement

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
in order to create a commotion throughout the courtyard,
as it is stated:
"We took sweet counsel together,
in the House of God we walked with the throng."
phrases.notes: The word ברגש ties to להרגיש, to stir up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּדֵי לְהַרְגִּישׁ כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the corrected question from step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lotteries were repeated to create a stir in the עזרה, based on 'בבית אלהים נהלך ברגש'.
steps.whatToRemember: There were several lotteries, not one, so that the עזרה would be filled with excitement.

steps.title: What clothes were worn for the lottery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כהנים were wearing while the lottery was held.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what do they hold the lottery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new practical question about the פייס: what clothing the כהנים wore. This sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery is not itself a service, but it is the first step toward the service. So it is unclear whether the כהנים had to be dressed in בגדי כהונה for it already.

keyTerms.meaning: In what? With what?

phrases.english: In what garments do they hold the lottery?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the same lottery topic
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which garments the כהנים wore during the פייס

steps.title: Weekday clothes or holy garments
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the כהנים wore weekday clothes, and רב ששת says they wore the holy בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: in weekday clothes. And רב ששת said: in holy garments.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question and disagree. One says regular clothes, and the other says בגדי קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two disagree about which danger the clothing rule guards against. The גמרא gives each one's reason in the next two steps. רב נחמן worries that כהנים who lost would force their way into the עבודה. רב ששת worries that an eager winner would serve without first changing into בגדי כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular, weekday clothing
The holy garments of the כהן
An אמורא who holds the lottery was in בגדי חול
An אמורא who holds the lottery was in בגדי קודש

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: in non-sacred garments,
and Rav Sheshet said: in sacred garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר בְּבִגְדֵי חוֹל וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר בְּבִגְדֵי קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 33 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: בגדי חול. רב ששת: בגדי קודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument leads into a discussion of whether it is allowed to wear בגדי כהונה when not doing a service.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason for weekday clothes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains why the lottery was held in weekday clothes. If the כהנים wore holy garments, strong men might grab the עבודה by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: they held the lottery in weekday clothes. If you say it was held in holy clothes, there are strong-armed men who would grab the job by force and do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason behind רב נחמן's opinion from step 34. The כהנים wore weekday clothes so that nobody was already dressed and ready to take over the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's worry is about people pushing in where they do not belong. If every כהן were already wearing בגדי כהונה, a strong כהן who lost the lottery could simply force his way in and serve. Weekday clothes act as a barrier: only the winner gets dressed and serves.

keyTerms.meaning: Weekday, non-holy clothes
Holy garments, the בגדי כהונה worn during the עבודה
Strong-armed men, people who use force
They grab or take by force

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new disagreement. Step 34 already gave the two opinions. Here the גמרא repeats רב נחמן's words to add his REASON.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: in weekday clothes,
because if you say in holy garments,
phrases.notes: Introduces the problem with the other option

phrases.english: there are strong-armed men
who would grab by force and perform the service.
phrases.notes: They would serve even though they lost the lottery

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב נחמן's view stated in step 34
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lottery is held in weekday clothes, so strong כהנים cannot force their way into the עבודה.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason for holy garments
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains why the lottery was held in holy garments. A winner in weekday clothes might rush to serve out of excitement and forget to change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: they held the lottery in holy garments. If you say it was held in weekday clothes, then out of their love for the עבודה, it could happen that they would go and serve right away, still in weekday clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason behind רב ששת's opinion. He worries that a happy winner might jump into the עבודה without first putting on בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's worry is the opposite of רב נחמן's. He is not afraid of the losers pushing in. He is afraid the winner will be so eager that he forgets to change, which would make the עבודה invalid. If everyone is already in holy garments, that mistake cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, due to
His love or eagerness for something precious (here, the עבודה)
It may happen, by accident
They perform the service

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions guard against two different dangers: force by the losers (רב נחמן) versus a careless mistake by the winner (רב ששת).

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: in holy garments,
because if you say in weekday clothes,
due to how beloved it is to them,
phrases.notes: Because the עבודה is so precious to them

phrases.english: it may happen that they would perform the service.
phrases.notes: Meaning they would serve while still in weekday clothes, which is invalid

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning, parallel in structure to רב נחמן's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lottery is held in holy garments, so an eager winner does not serve in weekday clothes by mistake.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings proof from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן proves his view from a משנה. After the lottery, the attendants stripped the כהנים of their clothes, leaving only the trousers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? We learned in a משנה: they handed the כהנים over to the attendants. The attendants would take their clothes off them and leave only the trousers on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן now supports his opinion with a משנה. It describes the כהנים being undressed after the lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים were already wearing holy garments during the lottery, there would be no reason to strip their clothes off before the עבודה. The fact that the attendants removed their clothes shows they were wearing weekday clothes, just as רב נחמן said. The trousers were left on, so they were never fully uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introduces a proof)
As we learned in a משנה
Attendants or officials of the Temple
They would undress, take clothes off
Trousers (one of the priestly garments)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: weekday clothes, to stop strong כהנים from forcing their way in. רב ששת: holy garments, so an eager winner does not serve in the wrong clothes. רב נחמן's proof: the משנה says the כהנים were undressed after the lottery.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From where do I say this?
As we learned: they handed them over to the attendants
and they would take their clothes off them,
and they would not leave on them
anything except the trousers alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן supports the view he explained in step 35 with a source from a משנה
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that the lottery was held in weekday clothes
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה stating that after the lottery the attendants removed the כהנים' clothes, leaving only the trousers
